name: Generate, email, and archive PDFs from HTML with PDFBolt, Gmail, and Google Drive
description:
## Quick overview
This workflow receives an HTML payload from an n8n webhook, validates it, converts HTML to PDF with PDFBolt, emails the PDF through Gmail, archives it in Google Drive, and returns a JSON response with success or error details.

## How it works
1. Receives HTML and delivery details through an n8n webhook.
2. Validates required fields and prepares the filename, email subject, and message.
3. Returns a 400 JSON error response if html or recipientEmail is missing.
4. Converts HTML to PDF with PDFBolt using the Direct endpoint.
5. Sends the generated PDF as an email attachment through Gmail to the specified recipient.
6. Uploads the same PDF binary file to a chosen Google Drive folder for archiving.
7. Returns a JSON success response to the webhook caller with the recipient email and filename.

## Setup
1. Install the PDFBolt community node and add your PDFBolt API key from https://app.pdfbolt.com/api-keys.
2. Add Gmail credentials in n8n for sending emails.
3. Add Google Drive credentials in n8n and select the target Drive and folder for archiving.
4. Activate the workflow and copy the Production webhook URL into the app or script that will POST the HTML payload.

## Requirements
- PDFBolt account and API key
- Gmail account connected in n8n
- Google Drive account connected in n8n
- App, script, or service that can send a POST request

## Customization
- Change the email subject and message from the webhook payload
- Choose a different Google Drive folder for archived PDFs
- Adjust PDF options in the PDFBolt node, such as page format or print background
- Extend the Code node to validate more fields or map a different payload structure

## Additional info
PDFBolt creates the PDF in the binary field data. Gmail and Google Drive use that field for the attachment and upload, so keep the field name unchanged unless you update those nodes too.

workflow.name: Generate, email, and archive PDFs from HTML with PDFBolt

parameters.content:
## Generate, email, and archive PDFs from HTML with PDFBolt

This workflow receives HTML from an app through an n8n webhook, validates the request, generates a PDF with PDFBolt, emails the PDF to a recipient, archives the same file in Google Drive, and returns a JSON response to the caller.

### Setup
1. Install the PDFBolt community node.
2. Add your PDFBolt API key from https://app.pdfbolt.com/api-keys.
3. Connect Gmail and Google Drive credentials in n8n.
4. Choose the Google Drive folder in the archive node.
5. Activate the workflow and send JSON to the Production webhook URL.

Use this when another app already creates HTML and n8n handles PDF generation, delivery, and archiving.

## Example webhook payload Send a POST request with JSON like this: ```json { "html": "

Quarterly Report

Generated from webhook data.

", "filename": "quarterly-report.pdf", "recipientEmail": "customer@example.com", "recipientName": "Example Customer", "emailSubject": "Your quarterly report", "emailMessage": "Hi Example Customer,\n\nPlease find your report attached.\n\nThank you." } ``` The workflow requires `html` and `recipientEmail`. If either field is missing, it returns a structured error response instead of trying to generate a PDF.

## Validate request
The Code node checks required fields, normalizes the PDF filename, prepares email text, and sends invalid requests to the error response branch.

## Generate, send, and archive
PDFBolt uses the Direct endpoint and returns the PDF as binary field `data`. Gmail sends that binary field as an attachment. Google Drive uploads the same binary field for archiving.
